description:
The Filter stage of DRA scheduler plugin makes a big latency if the pod count is large, In our tests, we have 5000 pods, running on 5000 nodes, each nodes has a ResourceSlice of GPU resources. the schedule time is about 10 minutes.

We found that the most of the schedule time is in Filter stage, and we also found that GatherPools is frequently on the top of the goroutine stack, so we checked the codes in GatherPools, found that there is a loop of slices there.

```
	for _, slice := range slices {
		....
	}
```
We have 5000 slices so it has to loop 5000 times for every Filter, and we have 5000 pods to schedule on 5000 nodes, so we will have to execute millions times of Filter.

In this PR, we will split the slices into two kinds, Shared and OnNode, we can use a map to store those OnNode and we can directly get the the OnNode slices directly when we has to execute Filter of Pod on a Node.

Also I think we can assume that most of the ResourceSlices is OnNode, and the Shared ResourceSlices should be a small portion.


#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug


#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This PR can reduce the DRA scheduling time for 5000 pods from 10min to 5min

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
None

comments.body:
This looks like a useful optimization, thanks for investigating and the detailed explanation in the PR.

We need to decide where and when to land this: Are we confident enough that we can use this immediately for most Kubernetes configurations or should it be treated as "experimental"?

This looks obvious enough that it can go into both "incubating" and "experimental" at the same time.

@mortent: thoughts?

I'm paranoid: this indirectly modifies the `alloc.slicesOnNode[node.Name]` slice by adding more elements in the underlying vector. This should be okay because only a single goroutine will ever do Filter for the given node, but this is a bit speculative and might not always be how this code is called.

I'd be more comfortable with:

```suggestion
	resourceSlices := slices.Concat(alloc.slicesOnNode[node.Name], alloc.slicesShared)
```

See also https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136619. Let's merge that first.

/hold

Once it's merged, we have two options here:
- Update only `experimental`.
- Update `experimental` and `incubating`.

The latter increases the blast radius of a potential bug or side effect of this change - but of course also makes it available in more cluster configurations.

I saw the panic in the job. Why can `node` be nil?

We might better fix callers which pass nil instead of working around that here.

There are some test cases such as "many-devices-okay" and "all-devices-invalid-CEL", which has no "node" defined in fields of the test case. I'm not sure if it is on purpose.
and also I found other codes when refer to the "node",  it will always check if it is nil.

It didn't matter, but now it does.

Instead of adding a "node" field to all test cases, let's fall back to a default node when a test case defines none.
Can you help me understand why we are checking `slicesForNode` here if we already know these slices are for the node?
Oh I think I kinda understand. slicesForNode is slicesOnNode + slicesShared.
Doesn't that mean we don't have to check slicesOnNode again since they will for sure match to the node?

> Doesn't that mean we don't have to check slicesOnNode again since they will for sure match to the node?

Yes, but so that `GatherPools` has to add another param,  it will have params like `slicesOnNode`, `slicesShared`, `allSlices`, It seems there are too many params for this function, and I think it is not a big cost to check the slicesOnNode again as it won't be many.

But I will add it if you think it is necessary, what do you guys think? @pohly @troychiu
I like this approach and I would feel pretty comfortable with us adding this to both `experimental` and `incubating`.
I think what you mentioned also makes sense to me. I am okay with either. Thank you.
@pohly as #136619  is merged, is this PR ready to be merged too?

Yes, let's merge it now.

/hold cancel

As nothing ever calls this with `node == nil`, the if check can be removed, which simplifies the code to a single call:

```patch
diff --git a/staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/structured/internal/experimental/allocator_experimental.go b/staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/structured/internal/experimental/allocator_experimental.go
index b3b711f9f82..60433862d5a 100644
--- a/staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/structured/internal/experimental/allocator_experimental.go
+++ b/staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/structured/internal/experimental/allocator_experimental.go
@@ -162,11 +162,7 @@ func (a *Allocator) Allocate(ctx context.Context, node *v1.Node, claims []*resou
 		result:               make([]internalAllocationResult, len(claims)),
 		allocatingCapacity:   NewConsumedCapacityCollection(),
 	}
-	var slicesForNode []*resourceapi.ResourceSlice
-	if node != nil {
-		slicesForNode = append(slicesForNode, alloc.slicesOnNode[node.Name]...)
-	}
-	slicesForNode = append(slicesForNode, alloc.slicesShared...)
+	slicesForNode := slices.Concat(alloc.slicesOnNode[node.Name], alloc.slicesShared)
 	alloc.logger.V(5).Info("Starting allocation", "numClaims", len(alloc.claimsToAllocate), "numSlices", len(slicesForNode))
 	defer func() {
 		alloc.logger.V(5).Info("Done with allocation", "success", len(finalResult) == len(alloc.claimsToAllocate), "err", finalErr)
diff --git a/staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/structured/internal/incubating/allocator_incubating.go b/staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/structured/internal/incubating/allocator_incubating.go

+++ b/staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/structured/internal/incubating/allocator_incubating.go
@@ -162,11 +162,7 @@ func (a *Allocator) Allocate(ctx context.Context, node *v1.Node, claims []*resou
 		result:               make([]internalAllocationResult, len(claims)),
 		allocatingCapacity:   NewConsumedCapacityCollection(),
 	}
-	var slicesForNode []*resourceapi.ResourceSlice
-	if node != nil {
-		slicesForNode = append(slicesForNode, alloc.slicesOnNode[node.Name]...)
-	}
-	slicesForNode = append(slicesForNode, alloc.slicesShared...)
+	slicesForNode := slices.Concat(alloc.slicesOnNode[node.Name], alloc.slicesShared)
 	alloc.logger.V(5).Info("Starting allocation", "numClaims", len(alloc.claimsToAllocate), "numSlices", slicesForNode)
 	defer func() {
 		alloc.logger.V(5).Info("Done with allocation", "success", len(finalResult) == len(alloc.claimsToAllocate), "err", finalErr)
```
